audit.why: Emerald+ 54.95% over 364 games. The packet flags the chart as contradicting that number, but a lane chart and a game win rate are different things: Aurora owns levels 1-6 and Aurelion Sol wins from the first item on. Rows 0-3 left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three chart rows disagreed across the layers. Full phases[4].side, phases[5].side and phases[6].side all said 'Skill'; content win[4] said 'Aurora' and win[5]/win[6] said 'Aurelion Sol'.
audit.why: The packet levelChart is Aurora at Level 6 and Aurelion Sol at First item and 2+ items. Level 6 is hers because Between Worlds is a leap plus a slow field she can teleport across — she picks both ends of the ground while Falling Star is a single 120s stun. From the first item the stardust curve is permanent and her poke is not.
audit.corrected: phases[4].side moves to 'Aurora' and its why is rewritten in the same proposal to argue for Aurora instead of describing Falling Star as a swing point. phases[5].side and phases[6].side move to 'Aurelion Sol', whose whys already argue for him. Rating on row 4 left at 6/10, matching row 3's existing Aurora/6-10.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entire content layer named abilities that are not Aurora's. It used 'Twin Disciplines' for her passive, 'Passage' for her W and 'The Weird Fate' for her R, across whys[1], whys[4], whys[5], spikes[0], spikes[1], spikes[2], early, mid, late, wants.you[1], wants.you[2], wants.foe[0], wants.foe[1] and wants.foe[2].
audit.why: Her real kit is Spirit Abjuration (P), Twofold Hex (Q), Across the Veil (W), The Weirding (E), Between Worlds (R). None of the three names on the page exist on her — 'Twin Disciplines' is another champion's passive entirely, and its description on the page ('alternates magic and physical damage') is that other champion's mechanic, not anything Aurora does. The packet's own defect list flags exactly this.
audit.corrected: Every instance replaced with the real ability and the real mechanic behind it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Between Worlds was described as a 'leash-and-follow mechanic' that lets her 'leash and follow through walls'. It does neither.
audit.why: Riot's R text: she leaps, releases a shockwave that damages and slows, then creates an area that slows enemies inside it and lets Aurora teleport from one side of that area to the other. There is no leash and no wall traversal. The counterplay the page taught — 'don't extend near walls or brush where she can set up the ultimate combo' — is aimed at a mechanic that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Rewritten in whys[4], spikes[1], phases[4].why and content mid around the slow field and the teleport across it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twofold Hex's recast was never mentioned, so the actual dodge was never taught.
audit.why: Riot's Q text: the missile curses enemies it hits, and the RECAST draws the active curses back toward her, damaging anyone in the way. Sidestepping the outgoing missile is only half of it — the return line is where the damage is, and it travels toward her, so stepping laterally beats stepping backward.
audit.corrected: Stated in dosFull[2].d, report[5].t and content early.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit Abjuration's healing was absent, and so was any anti-heal instruction.
audit.why: Her spells and attacks exorcise spirits that follow her and heal her, so a chip-damage war — which is Aurelion Sol's only pattern — refunds itself on her side. Grievous Wounds timing is what decides extended trades, and the itemisation line never mentioned it.
audit.corrected: Added to dontsFull[0].d, dontsFull[2].d, breakdown.carry and report[8].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: Aurora cancelling Aurelion Sol's channels was never stated.
audit.why: Breath of Light and Astral Flight are both interruptible channels, and Between Worlds carries hard CC. The Weirding's slow does not cancel them but it decides whether you can leave afterwards.

Across the Veil is 22s at rank 1 and drops only to 18s at rank 5; Twofold Hex is 9s at rank 1; The Weirding 15s; Between Worlds 140s at rank 1. Astral Flight is also 22s at rank 1, so her escape and your escape refresh together.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with the Across the Veil and Astral Flight numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed: dosFull[1].d ('Hold R as the anti-dive stun post-6') was the tradeGood string and dontsFull[2].d ('Trade HP for stacks below half health') was the tradeBad string.
audit.why: Both bodies now explain their own titles.
audit.corrected: dosFull[1].d rewritten around Falling Star's 120s and Between Worlds' 250-range leap; dontsFull[2].d around her spirit healing versus his complete lack of sustain.

audit.why: Male-enemy template with the name swapped in.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mechanical lint pass (tools/matchup-lint.js) over aurelionsol_mid: female enemies referred to as he/him/his in prose fields, breakdown.cooldowns fields containing no cooldown number, Do/Don't bodies that were the generic tradeGood/tradeBad string pasted under an unrelated title, "doubles" magnitude claims with no number, and report[4].t still holding the pre-audit template while breakdown.wave had been rewritten.

notes: This was the worst content file in my slice. Aurora's entire ability set was written under three names that are not hers — 'Twin Disciplines' (another champion's passive, described with that champion's alternating-damage mechanic), 'Passage' and 'The Weird Fate' — across fifteen fields. The packet's defect list already flagged that none of her real abilities (Spirit Abjuration, Twofold Hex, Across the Veil, The Weirding, Between Worlds) were ever named, and that is now fixed. On top of the names, Between Worlds was given a 'leash-and-follow through walls' mechanic it does not have, and the counterplay built on it ('don't extend near walls where she can set up the ultimate combo') was therefore advice about an imaginary ability. Chart: three rows disagreed between layers; I moved Level 6 to Aurora and rewrote its why in the same proposal, and moved First item and 2+ items to Aurelion Sol where their whys already argued for him. Unverified and left alone: whether Across the Veil's invisibility is stealth or camouflage in the ward/sweeper sense (Riot's text says 'becoming invisible', which I did not translate into ward advice); whether The Weirding's backward hop can be cancelled; whether Falling Star's stun can be Flash-buffered; tenacity/QSS on Between Worlds. The pre-rework 'Comet' language for Aurelion Sol appears here too (spikes[3], late, wants.you[2]) — fifth of five matchups so far.
